Technology

One container,end to end.

What happens between a depositor putting a bottle in and a reprocessor buying the material back. Each step carries the specification that governs it.

01

Deposit

The depositor feeds a single container into the intake. One at a time, upright or on its side — the machine indexes it onto the transport before anything else happens.

02

Identify

A barcode read establishes which product it is. In parallel, near-infrared sensing reads the polymer and an inductive sensor detects metal, so the machine knows the material even if the label is damaged.

First-pass recognition rate
—
source pending · pending
03

Validate

The read is checked against the register of deposit-bearing containers, and the container is checked for shape and emptiness. Anything unrecognised is handed straight back rather than swallowed.

Average deposit cycle per container
—
source pending · pending
04

Return value

Accepted containers are credited to the depositor at the machine — the reason they came. Value is redeemable in the store, which is what turns a return trip into a shopping trip.

Value returned per container
—

05

Sort by stream

The container is diverted to its own path on the strength of the material read: PET one way, aluminium the other. Sorting happens here, before anything is crushed, because a compacted mixed mass cannot be separated.

Stream separation purity
—
source pending · pending
06

Compact

Each stream is compacted its own way. PET is perforated and flattened so it cannot be re-inflated and claimed twice; cans are pressed flat. This is what makes a collection worth sending a vehicle for.

Compaction ratio
—
source pending · pending
07

Store

Compacted material drops into a separate bin per stream, never a single mixed hopper. Fill level is monitored continuously, so a collection is scheduled against real volume rather than a calendar.

08

Collect and report

Green Exchange collects on a route driven by fill level. Every accepted container is already counted, so the site receives volumes by stream and machine availability without anyone tallying anything.

09

Bale and offtake

Material is baled by stream at a processing centre, not in the store, then sold to a reprocessor. Separation quality upstream is what the bale is priced on.

10 Order of operations

Why sorting comes before compaction.

The sequence is not a preference. Once two materials are pressed into one mass they cannot be separated again at any price a reprocessor will pay, so every decision the machine makes about material happens while the container is still a container.

Identify first

Two independent reads — polymer by near-infrared, metal by induction — so a damaged label does not decide the outcome.

Divert second

PET and aluminium take separate paths from the diverter onward, with a compactor and a bin on each.

Compact last

PET is perforated so it cannot be re-inflated and claimed twice. Cans are pressed flat. Volume drops; stream purity does not.

NoteRejected containers are handed back rather than swallowed, and are never counted. A count that included them would overstate recovery on the first day of operation.
